userPrompt:
Run the agent in a container that Suspense owns, so each mode sees only what
it may use. The isolation comes from what is mounted, not from prompts, deny
rules or guards. Spec tasks, a chain's spec step and questions always run
this way. Code tasks and a chain's code step run this way only when the
project's "Run code tasks in a container" option is on (off by default); when
it is off they run on the host as today, with the mode guard and read-deny
rule.

Why: Spec work keeps reading and even changing code, which wastes time and
tokens, and the chain's code step then finds nothing to do. Deny rules and
prompt wording are only nudges, because a shell can read anything. A
container that has no code in it can't read the code or change it, whatever
the harness is and whatever it tries.

What should be true afterwards:

1. Container runtime: Podman only, run through the `podman` CLI. Each run is
   one `podman run --rm` of the agent's command, a child of the app, so
   stopping a task stops its container. On Linux it runs rootless with the
   user's id (--userns=keep-id), so files it writes belong to the user. On
   macOS and Windows, Podman runs in a `podman machine`.
   - If `podman` isn't installed, a Spec, Chain or Ask prompt isn't sent, and
     there is no unisolated fallback. The task or question says Podman is
     needed and links to Podman's installation instructions for the platform
     it's running on: https://podman.io/docs/installation#macos on macOS,
     https://podman.io/docs/installation#windows on Windows, and
     https://podman.io/docs/installation#installing-on-linux on Linux. It's
     reported the way a missing harness or missing piton is today.
   - On macOS and Windows, if no Podman machine exists or it isn't running,
     the task says so and offers to set it up (`podman machine init`) or
     start it (`podman machine start`), showing the output in its raw stream.
   - Code tasks with the project option on need Podman in the same way. With
     the option off, they never need it.

2. Image. Suspense builds a default image and keeps it up to date: the
   harness CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) and piton, the same versions
   as on the host where it can find them. A project can provide its own
   Containerfile (.suspense/Containerfile) built FROM the default to add
   toolchains, and Suspense builds and caches it when it changes, with
   `podman build`. While an image is building, the task shows "Preparing
   environment" and the output goes to its raw stream.

3. What each run sees. Mounts are made at the same absolute paths as on the
   host where the platform allows, so paths in tool events need no mapping.
   Where they can't be (macOS, Windows), container paths are mapped back to
   host paths everywhere they are shown or opened (referenced-spec sidebar,
   file links, understanding file, files changed).
   - Spec task, chain spec step: the spec location rw, the compiled
     reference rw, the fluency file ro, piton.config.pi ro, and the task's
     understanding file rw. No code location.
   - Question (Ask): the code location ro, the compiled reference ro, and
     piton.config.pi ro. No spec source. Nothing writable but the harness's
     own volumes.
   - Code task, chain code step, with the option on: the code location rw,
     the compiled reference ro, piton.config.pi ro, and the understanding
     file rw. No spec source.
   Nothing else from the host is mounted: no home directory, no user-level
   skills, MCP servers or ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, no git directory. Snapshots,
   diffs, files changed and commits are still done by Suspense on the host.

4. Persistent Podman volumes, owned and named by Suspense:
   - one per harness for its login and settings (~/.claude, ~/.codex,
     OpenCode's data directory), shared by every project, so a harness is
     logged in once for all of them;
   - one per project and conversation lane (spec lane, code lane,
     questions) for the harness's sessions, so each lane can resume its own
     conversation;
   - caches per project (e.g. cargo registry and target directory) for
     containerised Code runs.
   Losing a volume costs only a login or a cache, never project data.

5. Logging in. When a harness in its volume isn't logged in, Suspense runs
   its login command in the container under a pseudo-terminal and shows a
   login view. It opens any login URL the CLI prints in the host's browser.
   Where the CLI asks for a pasted code, the view has a field for it, which
   goes to the PTY. Where it waits for a localhost callback on a known port,
   that port is published for the login run. Where it offers device-code
   login, that is used. Credentials stay in the harness's volume and are
   refreshed there, so login happens once per machine, not per run. The
   Settings window shows each harness's container login state and has a
   "Log in again" action.

6. Conversations by lane. Spec lane tasks (Spec tasks and chain spec steps)
   carry on a conversation of their own, separate from the code lane's, so
   nothing a code task read reaches a spec task. Questions keep their own
   conversation as today. The chain handoff stays as text (the prompt and
   the spec step's reply), so it crosses lanes unchanged. New conversation
   resets the lane it is used from.

7. The spec build. A Spec run's agent can run `piton build` inside its
   container (the code location isn't there, so shape outputs written into
   it are discarded). After every Spec or chain spec step, Suspense runs the
   real `piton build` on the host as it does before sending, so the host's
   reference and shape outputs are current.

8. Prompts describe only what the run can see. For containerised runs, the
   system template, the spec-reading prompt and the mode instructions no
   longer name a location the run can't see, or tell it not to read or edit
   one: Spec and chain-spec-step instructions don't name the code location,
   and Ask and containerised Code instructions say the spec is read from
   the compiled reference without naming the spec source. The shared system
   prompt stays identical within a lane's conversation, so the prompt cache
   holds.

9. Guards. A containerised run has no mode guard, no read-deny rule and no
   edit-deny rule: nothing to protect is mounted. Host runs (Code with the
   option off, Freeform) keep them as today.

10. Project option. "Run code tasks in a container" is a per-project
    setting, saved with the project as the ProjectDataScope says, shown in
    the Settings window, off by default. Turning it on applies from the next
    Code or chain code step.

Spec: harness-integration (how a run is started, conversations and
resuming, Claude Code's flags), prompt-mode/index and prompt-mode/sending
(lanes, chains, the pre-send build, the mode guard), prompt-mode/
mode-system-prompts (what each mode's prompts say), project-data (the new
option, Containerfile, and which data is the project's vs. Suspense's),
settings-window (the option and the harness login state), and spec-build
(the build after a spec step). Update those anchors rather than adding
parallel ones. Add one new scope for the container environment (Podman,
the missing-Podman and machine states with their platform install links,
image, mounts per mode, volumes, login), and link to it from the others.

Code: put the container environment in its own module (Podman detection and
machine state, platform install links, image build and cache, mounts per
mode, volume names, path mapping, the login PTY flow), used by
src/harness.rs where the agent's Command is built, for send, one-off runs
and ask_quickly alike when their mode is containerised. Update
src/mode_guard.rs so containerised runs aren't guarded, src/system_prompts.rs
and .suspense/system-prompts/*.md for the prompt wording, the conversation
bookkeeping in src/prompt_mode.rs and src/conversations.rs for the separate
spec-lane conversation, src/settings_window.rs for the option and login
state, and src/referenced_spec.rs and src/shell_paths.rs for path mapping.
Tests: mounts per mode (Spec has no code mount, Ask has no spec mount and
nothing rw, Code only with the option on), the missing-Podman error linking
to the right install page per platform, the machine-not-running state on
macOS and Windows, the spec lane resuming its own conversation, no guard or
deny rule for containerised runs, and container-to-host path mapping. Use a
fake `podman` binary, as the existing tests use a fake harness.

1	//! Harness integration: sends a compiled prompt to a local coding harness as a
2	//! one-off run (`claude -p`, `codex exec`, or `opencode run`, whichever the
3	//! user picked) in the project directory, streaming what it does as it does
4	//! it. A run can resume the conversation of an earlier one, so the harness
5	//! keeps its context between prompts, and a task's run can be fed more
6	//! messages while it works, where the harness allows.
7	
8	use std::io::{BufRead as _, BufReader, Write as _};
9	use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
10	use std::process::{Child, ChildStdin, Command, Stdio};
11	use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
12	
13	use anyhow::{Context as _, Result, bail};
14	use futures::channel::mpsc;
15	use serde_json::{Value, json};
16	
17	use crate::agent::{self, Agent};
18	use crate::attached_image;
19	use crate::harness_mentions;
20	use crate::usage::{PlanLimit, Spend, Tally};
21	
22	/// The directory the harness in use reads its agentic Markdown and reference
23	/// files from, which a system prompt's `${HARNESS_DIRECTORY}` stands for.
24	pub fn directory() -> &'static str {
25	    agent::current().directory()
26	}
27	
28	/// Something the harness did, in the order it happened.
29	#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
30	pub enum HarnessEvent {
31	    /// The conversation the run is part of, which a later run can resume.
32	    Session(String),
33	    /// A raw line of the harness's output, sent before the events parsed
34	    /// from it.
35	    Output(String),
36	    /// A new block of reply text began.
37	    TextStarted,
38	    TextDelta(String),
39	    ToolStarted {
40	        id: String,
41	        name: String,
42	    },
43	    /// A tool call's input is known; `summary` is its most telling argument.
44	    ToolInput {
45	        id: String,
46	        summary: String,
47	    },
48	    ToolFinished {
49	        id: String,
50	        is_error: bool,
51	    },
52	    /// A tool call's whole input, from the run or from a subagent it started,
53	    /// for working out the files it names.
54	    ToolCalled {
55	        id: String,
56	        name: String,
57	        input: Value,

content.text:
The containerised runs are built and all 464 tests pass, with 4 test threads. I haven't run a real Claude Code task in a container end to end, and logging in has never actually been done. On real Podman I checked the generated `podman run` arguments with a throwaway Alpine container: the spec mount is writable, the code is read-only, the hidden folder appears empty, and files written belong to you (uid 1000).

**What runs where**
- **Always in a container:** Spec tasks, a Chain prompt's spec steps, and questions.
- **Only with "Run code tasks in a container" on:** Code tasks and a Chain prompt's code step. The option is saved in `.suspense/settings.json` and read when each task is sent.
- **Always on the host, as before:** Freeform and the app's own one-off runs, with the mode guard and read-deny rule unchanged.

**How a containerised run works**
- **The run:** each run is one `podman run --rm` child of the app, so stopping a task stops its container.
- **No guards:** it gets no mode guard and no deny rules. It still registers what it may write, so a guarded Code task running on the host beside it doesn't undo its changes.
- **Mounts:** only what each mode may see is mounted. A location sitting inside a mounted folder that the run mustn't see (the spec, `.suspense`, `.git`) is covered with an empty read-only folder. Read-only files that don't exist yet are left out, since Podman can't mount them.
- **Paths:** on Windows, container paths are mapped back to host paths for everything the harness reports. On Linux and macOS the mounts sit at the same paths, so nothing needs mapping.
- **Image:** Suspense builds a default image from the host's harness versions, plus a project image from `.suspense/Containerfile` when one exists. While building, the task shows "Preparing environment" and the build output goes to its raw stream.
- **Volumes:** one per harness for its login, one per project and lane for sessions, and one per project for caches.
- **When it can't run:** the task fails with a button. Without Podman it's "Install Podman", which opens your platform's install page. On macOS or Windows with no machine it's "Set up Podman", and with a stopped machine "Start Podman". If the harness isn't logged in it's "Log in". The task is resent once the machine starts or the login succeeds.
- **Login:** the login runs in a pseudo-terminal, opens any URL it prints in your browser, and has a field for pasting a code.
- **After a spec run:** `piton build` runs on the host, and the task shows "Building" meanwhile.

**Conversations and prompts**
- **Per lane:** the spec lane and code lane each carry on their own conversation. Changing the code option starts the code lane on a new one, because host and container sessions are stored in different places.
- **New conversation:** it resets the selected tab's lane, or both lanes on Chain.
- **Locations a run can't see:** they are filled in with nothing, and any paragraph naming them is dropped.
- **Default prompt files:** I rewrote the default prompts in `.suspense/system-prompts/*.md` so each location sits in its own paragraph. These are also this project's own prompts, so your next tasks will be worded this way.
- **Code-to-spec handoff:** it no longer tells a spec run to read the code, since its container has none.
- **Already-saved prompts:** a project whose prompts were saved earlier keeps the old wording. Its opening line names both locations, so a containerised run drops that whole paragraph and loses the sentence saying what the mode is for. Resetting the prompts in Settings fixes that.

**Settings:** a new Containers section shows Podman's state, each harness's container login with "Log in again", and the project checkbox.

**Where I went differently from your brief**
- **Path mapping:** it happens once, on each line the harness prints, rather than separately in `referenced_spec.rs` and `shell_paths.rs`. Everything downstream already sees host paths.
- **One-off runs and quick asks:** they stay on the host, because the spec gives them no mode.
- **Tests and Podman:** in tests, a run only goes through a container when the test stands in a fake `podman`, so the existing tests keep using their fake harness on the host.

**Tests added:** mounts per mode, which runs go in a container, the missing-Podman link on each platform, a missing or stopped machine on macOS and Windows, a containerised run through a fake `podman` with no deny rule, the spec lane resuming its own conversation, no guard for containerised runs, and container-to-host path mapping.

**Limits**
- **piton in the image:** it's copied in only on Linux. On macOS and Windows the image has no piton unless your project's Containerfile adds it, so a spec run can't build inside its container there. The host build afterwards still keeps the reference current.
- **Login and other platforms:** not tried for real, and nothing has been run on macOS or Windows.
- **Cache volume:** it is re-owned to you on every run, which may be slow once a Cargo target directory gets large.
- **Code location:** in this repository `codeRoot` is `./src` while `Cargo.toml` sits at the root, so a containerised Code task here couldn't build the crate.

**Left on your machine**
- **Four Podman volumes:** `suspense-home-claude`, `suspense-home-codex`, `suspense-home-opencode` and `suspense-sessions-…-questions` were created at 17:57 by my test runs checking login state through your real Podman. That run happened before I made tests never touch it. They should only hold what a "not logged in" status check writes, so they're safe to remove with `podman volume rm`. If your app has been running this code, a login there would have gone into them, so check before removing. I didn't delete them myself.
- **Images:** a `localhost/suspense-default` image was built 14 minutes before that, and `node:22-bookworm-slim` is present. I didn't build or remove either, so they may come from your own app run. The Alpine image I pulled for the check is removed.

The constraints are in `.suspense/history/1791022922-AgentContainerModeIsolation.understanding.md`.
